verdict.rationale: Claude ships an official desktop app (Mac, Windows, Linux via apt) and a Cowork/computer-use feature that lets Claude 'navigate to your screen directly—clicking, typing, and opening apps' while the user watches, which shows real screen access. However there is no evidence of dedicated OS-level keyboard shortcuts (e.g., a global hotkey to invoke Claude with current screen context) — the screen access described is agentic task automation rather than a power-user shortcut workflow. Missing for 10: documented OS-level global shortcuts/hotkeys, and evidence that a user can quickly summon Claude to see the current screen via keypress rather than launching a Cowork/computer-use task.
